title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the 1986 'third version' of Grothendieck's Analysis situs, an axiomatic attempt at the 'tame topology' announced in Esquisse d'un programme (§5).

The framework:
- M is a poset of objects (figures, models), ordered by ≤ ('is a closed subfigure of') and ≪ (a stronger, possibly 'contained/embedded' relation).
- F ⊂ M is the set of figures.
- L ⊂ M is the set of 'lieux': the minimal non-empty elements, which play the role of atoms or places.
- omb(X), the 'ombre' (shadow), is the set of lieux below X. omb(X)° is the set of lieux lying 'interiorly' in X, i.e. in an open stratum.
- X ∥ Y is the disjointness relation, called 'disjonction'.

The previous page set up the 'axiomes de divisibilité'. AtL1 (omb(X)° ≠ ∅ for X ∈ M) forces the lieux to be 'infinitely divisible', so they are not discrete points.

Ax L2 (criterion of disjointness by lieux). For X, Y ∈ M: X ∥ Y iff x ∥ y for all x ∈ omb(X) and y ∈ omb(Y). Grothendieck warns that this is not the same as omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = ∅. Distinct lieux are disjoint only under the stronger axiom At ens D (prev. page, Cor 3). Corollary: the same criterion holds for figures F, G ∈ F.

Ax L3 (disjointness axiom for lieux). For X, Y ∈ M with X ≠ Y (and, as written, X not ≤ Y, or not comparable; the hypothesis is ambiguous): any x in the interior shadow of X and y in the interior shadow of Y are disjoint. A margin note says it is equivalent to the following corollary, given L2.
- Corollary: for a figure F, two lieux lying in different (open) strata of F are disjoint. In other words, the interior shadows of the strata partition the shadow of F: this is the stratification-is-a-partition principle, expressed in point-free terms.
- NB: with Ax D it suffices to require L3 when Y ≤ X.

Ax CL(spéc) (criterion of compatibility, for neighbouring lieux). This rewrites the gluing/compatibility axiom Ax C(spéc) using L2.
- Setting: X, Y ∈ M, with L = X ∧ Y = Sup of the Z ≤ X, Y.
- Claim: X and Y are compatible, i.e. can be glued along L, provided every lieu of X not in omb(L) is disjoint from every lieu of Y not in omb(L).
- Justification: Ax spéc demands X' ∥ Y' for X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y with X'_L = Y'_L = ∅, where X'_L is the 'trace' of X' on L. By L2 this reduces to lieux x ≪ X', y ≪ Y'. The next page's Lemma 1 (for a lieu x ≪ Q and P ≤ Q, x_P = ∅ iff x ∉ omb(P)) turns the trace conditions into x ∉ omb(L) and y ∉ omb(L).
- Margin: 'on voudrait mieux pour : il faut et il suffit ?' He wants the criterion to be necessary as well as sufficient.

Purpose: to reduce the global disjointness and gluing axioms of a point-free theory of stratified 'tame' spaces to conditions on the atoms (lieux). This makes the lieux behave like points without being points.
errors: The hypothesis of Ax L3 is ambiguous in the manuscript. It reads like 'X ≰ Y (crossed or variant symbol), X ≠ Y'. Yet the NB says that under Ax D it suffices to treat the case Y ≤ X, so comparable pairs must be allowed. The intended hypothesis is probably just X ≠ Y, or a symmetric non-inclusion.

Ax CL(spéc) is only proved to be sufficient for compatibility, via Ax spéc and Lemma 1 of the next page. Grothendieck himself flags the converse ('il faut et il suffit ?') as open; nothing here establishes it.

The reduction uses L2 only in one direction plus Lemma 1, which assumes lieux are minimal for ≪ in M∖{∅}. That is fine, but the derivation silently uses L ≤ X and L ≤ Y, a point Grothendieck notes on the next page.

ideas.what: Disjointness of objects is detected on atoms ('lieux'), which are infinitely divisible and not points (Ax L2).
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / mereotopological separation; atom-detection of disjointness in a region-based geometry; cf. separating sets of points in locales
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead and de Laguna (region-based geometry), Tarski (geometry of solids), Clarke (connection calculus); locale theory by Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for a tame topology appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatic system is unpublished

ideas.what: Lieux in distinct open strata of a figure are disjoint (Ax L3 and its corollary): the stratification is a partition at the level of atoms.
ideas.modern_name: Partition property of stratifications (o-minimal cell decomposition, Whitney/Thom stratifications), here axiomatised point-free
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Łojasiewicz; for o-minimality van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight

ideas.what: Gluing/compatibility criterion along the meet L = X ∧ Y, expressed via disjointness of the atoms outside omb(L) (Ax CL(spéc)), with an open question whether it is necessary and sufficient.
ideas.modern_name: Gluing of stratified spaces along closed unions; a pushout/compatibility criterion in a poset of subobjects; cf. van Kampen-type or excision conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; classical for CW and polyhedral complexes (gluing along subcomplexes)

ideas.what: AtL1 / infinite divisibility read as the introduction of the 'actual infinite' into the axioms (previous page), used here to make lieux substitute for points.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Leśniewski, Tarski; in philosophy, Lewis and Sider on 'gunk'

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 system is an axiomatic, region-based (point-free) geometry. It has a disjointness relation ∥, a parthood order ≤/≪, minimal but infinitely divisible 'lieux', and the axiom that disjointness is tested on atoms. This is structurally very close to Whitehead–Tarski–Clarke mereotopology and to Boolean contact algebras. That literature has never been connected to Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, nor his to it.
missed.quote: X ∥ Y ⟺ ∀x ∈ omb(X), y ∈ omb Y, x ∥ y  (Ça ne signifie pas forcément omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = ∅ !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a ready-made logical and model-theoretic toolkit (contact algebras, representation theorems) for Grothendieck's unrealised axiomatic tame topology. Conversely, it gives mereotopology a geometric target: o-minimal or semialgebraic stratified sets.

missed.claim: Whether the atomic compatibility criterion CL(spéc) is also necessary for two models X, Y to be gluable along X ∧ Y is left open.
missed.quote: on voudrait mieux pour : il faut et il suffit ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A necessary-and-sufficient atomic gluing criterion would be a key structural lemma for any axiomatic (e.g. o-minimal or definable) theory of stratified spaces that is to be closed under gluing.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an unpublished, technically specific piece of Grothendieck's axiomatic tame topology: a point-free theory with infinitely divisible atoms and disjointness detected on atoms. The individual statements are elementary and partly routine. What is notable, and essentially absent from the literature, is the overall approach and its unremarked kinship with mereotopology. Still, nothing here is a striking finished result.
transcription_corrections: Heading of Ax L2: 'Critère de disposition par les lieux' is more likely 'Critère de disjonction par les lieux'; ∥ denotes disjointness. Similarly, Ax L3 is likely '(Axiome de disjonction pour les lieux)' rather than 'Additivité de disposition'.
'Cà une parfaitement non omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = ∅ !)' should read roughly '(Ça ne signifie pas forcément que omb(X) ∩ omb(Y) = ∅ !)'.
Corollary of L3: 'deux lieux opposés[?] des strates différentes de F sont disjointes' should be roughly 'deux lieux appartenant à des strates [ouvertes] différentes de F sont disjoints'.
In Ax L3 the hypothesis is written with a modified order symbol (X ≯/≰ Y) followed by 'X ≠ Y'. A first attempt ('X≠Y'?) is crossed out before it.
In Ax CL, 'pour des lieux [-polyédraux-] {+voisins+}' is a struck word with 'voisins' written above. The struck word is uncertain (possibly 'polyédraux').

'Alors pour que Z ∈ X ∧ Y' is a misplacement. 'Z ⊆ X∧Y' (or Z ≤ X, Y) is written under 'Sup Z' as the index of the sup, and the sentence reads 'Alors pour que X et Y soient compatibles, il suffit que ∀x ∈ omb(X) ∖ omb(L), y ∈ omb(Y) − omb(L), on a x ∥ y'.
Margin on L3: 'équivalent, moyennant L2'. Margin on CL: 'on voudrait mieux pour : il faut et il suffit ?'.
